exposure: Particulate air pollution (black carbon, PM2.5, coarse PM, PM10)
outcome: Intestinal microbiome alpha diversity (observed richness, species evenness, Shannon diversity)
cohort: 412 young children from the ENVIRONAGE cohort.
finding: The study revealed a sex-dependent association between particulate air pollution exposure and intestinal microbiome composition, indicating that boys may be more vulnerable to diversity loss associated with childhood exposure.
